post_text:
US chronic absenteeism was 15% before the pandemic.
It hit 28% at peak.
Right now, in 2024–25, it’s 22%.

We call that recovery.

Still 47% above pre-pandemic levels. Five states are actively moving backwards. Alaska is at 42.8%. Alabama recovered to within 0.9 points of its 2019 baseline.

The difference isn’t geography or poverty — it’s whether states built durable attendance infrastructure during COVID or spent relief money without building anything lasting.

46 states. 5 data snapshots. The recovery is real for some states. For others, a permanently worse normal has quietly become the baseline.
